name: Ujung Kulon National Park
blurb: Last home of the Javan rhino in Java's lowland rainforest and mangroves.

tip.title: Shrink the rhino feeding grounds
tip.text: Rhinos and banteng share a shrinking patch of feeding ground. Set Eupatorium to -80% and watch the rhino and banteng, then the dhole and leopard.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Ujung Kulon National Park, Javan rhinoceros, Asian water monitor). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Year-round warm sunshine drives growth in the rainforest canopy, clearings and mangroves.

nodes.name: Tropical rain
nodes.desc: Heavy rainfall keeps the lowland rainforest of the peninsula lush and the soils and swamps wet.
Leaf litter and dead animals are broken down and the nutrients return to the soil for plants to use.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Eupatorium (Siam weed)
nodes.desc: Leafy shrub that Wikipedia says Javan rhinos feed on. Its feeding grounds in the park shrank from 158 ha to 20 ha by 2013.
Figs are among the coastal and forest plants of the park and are a food source for fruit-eating birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses of open ground and clearings that feed grazing deer and cattle.

nodes.name: Javan rusa
nodes.desc: A deer of forest edges and open ground and the most recorded large mammal in the area.
Small forest deer that eats foliage and fallen fruit; recorded as prey of leopards and dholes.
A common monkey that eats fruit and is recorded eating the fruits of Aglaia and Antidesma.
Omnivore that roots in the soil and eats fruit. Recorded prey of leopards, dholes and pythons.
Fruit-eating forest civet recorded eating Aglaia fruit; leopards are recorded to prey on it.
Huge constrictor recorded taking monkeys, wild boar, mouse-deer and water monitors.

nodes.name: Asian water monitor
nodes.desc: Opportunistic large lizard that often scavenges carrion and also takes monkeys and small deer; recorded as prey of reticulated pythons.

nodes.name: Javan leopard
nodes.desc: Top predator of the peninsula since the Javan tiger disappeared in the mid-1960s. Recorded eating banteng, dhole, muntjac, civets and boar.
Pack-hunting wild dog that mainly takes medium and large hoofed animals; recorded taking banteng, muntjac and wild boar, and the Javan rusa is a named prey.

story: Ujung Kulon National Park covers the westernmost tip of Java, 1,056.95 km² of which 443.37 km² is marine. UNESCO cites it for containing the largest remaining area of lowland rainforest in Java.
matters: It is also cited for the Javan rhinoceros, the most threatened rhino species. The Javan rhino is critically endangered and one of five rhino species left.
